metadata.title: Cloud Firestore - SC-28 / SC-28(1) Component Definition
metadata.remarks: Platform-specific layer (3c), the GCP counterpart of the Azure SQL component definition (3b). Describes how Cloud Firestore meets SC-28 and SC-28(1) and which technology-agnostic rules verify it. The rules and their checks are defined once, in the imported datastore-checks component definition (3a); this file only references their Rule_Ids. Organisation parameter values live in the organisation profile (2b, the source below); the sc-28_odp.01 selection and system-specific values live in the SSP. The GCP adapter (automation/gcp_terraform_inventory.py) maps this component onto the datastore inventory that the checks read.

components.title: Cloud Firestore
components.description: Google Cloud Firestore document database. Firestore encrypts all data before it is written to disk, with no configuration required and no option to turn it off; keys are Google-managed by default, and customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK, Cloud KMS) can be chosen only when a database is created. Firestore has no cryptographic tamper-evidence (ledger) feature.

control-implementations.description: SC-28 and SC-28(1) implementation for Cloud Firestore data at rest, against the organisation profile.

implemented-requirements.description: Confidentiality of data at rest: Firestore server-side encryption, always on (verified by datastore_encrypted_at_rest). Integrity of data at rest: not provided by Firestore itself; datastore_tamper_evident can only pass if a tamper-evidence mechanism is added outside Firestore.

sc-28.1_obj-1 (disclosure): Firestore encrypts all stored data with Google-managed keys by default, or with a customer-managed Cloud KMS key if the database was created with CMEK (datastore_encrypted_at_rest). sc-28.1_obj-2 (modification): Firestore offers no cryptographic tamper evidence, so the organisation guidance for obj-2 cannot be met by Firestore configuration alone (datastore_tamper_evident fails); it needs an added mechanism, such as an application-maintained hash chain with digests held outside Firestore, or a different datastore.

components.remarks: Datastore inventory mapping used by the GCP adapter for google_firestore_database: encryption_at_rest.enabled is always true (server-side encryption cannot be disabled); tamper_evidence.enabled is always false (no tamper-evidence feature). Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/docs/server-side-encryption and https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/docs/cmek (checked 2026-11-22).
